append.text: **Ps 139:2 (twice), 139:5 *Éripe me, Dómine, ab hómine malo: a viro iníquo éripe me … et ab homínibus iníquis éripe me* → *Arrancai-me, Senhor, do homem mau: * do homem iníquo arrancai-me … e dos homens iníquos arrancai-me*** — a source named each time, so the row's *arrancar*; the CNBB LH and Ave Maria's *Livrai-me* are liberáre's verb here. The versicle (Preces at Prime, Passiontide None) and the Offertory of Holy Tuesday (139:5) follow; see the formula row. No reader remarked.

**Ps 139:3, 139:5b, 139:9 *Qui cogitavérunt iniquitátes … Qui cogitavérunt supplantáre … cogitavérunt contra me* → *Os que maquinaram iniquidades … Os que maquinaram derrubar … maquinaram contra mim*** — a fifth vote for the *maquinar* split (hostile or evil object, three times in one psalm). Passed the Latinist twice; no reader remarked.

**Ps 139:5b *Qui cogitavérunt supplantáre gressus meos* → *Os que maquinaram derrubar os meus passos*** — draft 1 took the row's option *fazer tropeçar*; the v1 stylist heard *tropeçar* (5b) and *tropeço* (6b, scándalum) as one root twice where the Latin has two words, and the row's *derrubar* was taken (with *gressus* as 36:31). The v2 Latinist (minor) asked *fazer tropeçar* back for the heel-trip image; refused for the echo, held as the option.

Ps 139:5b *abscondérunt láqueum mihi* → *esconderam um laço para mim*; 139:6 *funes extendérunt in láqueum* → *estenderam cordas em laço* (*in* + acc. of purpose kept, as 68:23). No reader heard a ribbon.
Ps 139:6 *Et funes extendérunt in láqueum* → *E estenderam cordas em laço* — the row; no remark.
**Ps 139:6 *juxta iter scándalum posuérunt mihi* → *junto do caminho puseram um tropeço para mim*** — the row applied; the reason 139:5b's supplantáre is *derrubar*, not *fazer tropeçar*.

**Ps 139:8 *Dómine, Dómine, virtus salútis meæ* → *Senhor, Senhor, poder da minha salvação*** — God's virtus → *poder*; the Thursday Vespers antiphon (*Ne derelínquas me, * Dómine, virtus salútis meæ*) and the Matins antiphon *Inténde in adjutórium meum, * Dómine, virtus salútis meæ* carry the phrase — see the formula row. No remark.

Ps 139:8 *obumbrásti super caput meum in die belli* → *fizestes sombra sobre a minha cabeça no dia da guerra* (*super* → *sobre*; *bellum → guerra*, kept apart from 139:3 *prǽlia → batalhas*). The stylist offered *cobristes de sombra a minha cabeça* (option).
**Ps 139:11 *Cadent super eos carbónes* → *Cairão sobre eles carvões*** — the row (the verse it names); *brasas* not asked by any reader here.

**Ps 139:11 *in ignem deícies eos* → *ao fogo os lançareis*** — a local departure: *abater no fogo* was heard as slaughtering (stylist) and loses the motion of *in ignem* (Latinist minor); *lançar* is the casting down into. *abatereis* option.
**Ps 139:10 *labor labiórum ipsórum opériet eos* → *a fadiga dos seus lábios os cobrirá*** — draft 1 *o trabalho* was heard as 'a job description' (stylist); the row's word taken. No further remark.

**Ps 139:12 *Vir linguósus non dirigétur in terra* → *O homem de língua solta não será dirigido na terra*** — held (the straight course, κατευθυνθήσεται); the stylist offered *firmado* (Almeida's *não terá firmeza*), kept as option.
**Ps 139:12 *virum injústum mala cápient in intéritu* → *os males tomarão o homem injusto na destruição*** (θηρεύσει, as 58:4) — held; the stylist's *apanharão … na ruína* kept as option.
Ps 139:12 *in intéritu* → *na destruição* — the row; no remark.
**Ps 139:13 *judícium ínopis* → *o juízo do carente*** (D38) — the stylist asked *desvalido* (Ave Maria's word here); kept under D38, option. More cost evidence.

**Ps 139:14 *habitábunt recti cum vultu tuo* → *os retos habitarão com o vosso rosto*** (as 20:7 *com o vosso rosto*) — the stylist asked *junto ao vosso rosto* (option); the Latinist, twice, praised the Latin's reading kept.
Ps 139:14 *Verúmtamen justi confitebúntur nómini tuo* → *Todavia, os justos darão graças ao vosso nome* — the row; no remark.
Ps 139:13 *Cognóvi quia fáciet Dóminus* → *Eu sei que o Senhor fará* — the proposal applied (*quia*, no time-word); no remark.

**Ps 139:3 *tota die constituébant prǽlia* → *o dia todo armavam batalhas*** — a local departure: *estabelecer batalhas* is not Portuguese; *armar* (MS1932 *armam combates*) sets up a fight, παρετάσσοντο. *estabeleciam* option.

**Ps 139:4b *venénum áspidum sub lábiis eórum* → *veneno de áspides debaixo dos seus lábios*** — the third colon word for word, verbless; passed the Latinist twice. The ambiguity reader listed *áspides* unknown. First colon *Afiaram as suas línguas como a da serpente* (63:4's verb, 57:5's genitive).
**Ps 139:7 *Dixi Dómino: Deus meus es tu* → *Eu disse ao Senhor: Vós sois o meu Deus*** — the formula held; the stylist named 139:7 the best verse.

terms: | linguósus | de língua solta (*O homem de língua solta não será dirigido na terra*) | open | Ps 139:12, a psalter hapax (γλωσσώδης; L&S 'talkative'). Draft 1 *linguarudo* (one word for one) was heard as 'a gossip' by the ambiguity reader and as familiar by the stylist; *de língua solta* keeps the tongue and the loose talk. DRB 'a man full of tongue'; MS1932 *O caluniador*, Almeida *de má língua* (the Hebrew's) — options. |

| *a desidério meo* (+ dat.) | do meu desejo (*Não me entregueis, Senhor, do meu desejo ao pecador*) | open | Ps 139:9 (ἀπὸ τῆς ἐπιθυμίας μου, the Greek's misreading of the Hebrew). Kept as open as the Latin (DRB 'from my desire'); the ambiguity reader heard noise — the Latin's own opacity. The stylist's order *… ao pecador, Senhor, do meu desejo* refused (a vocative 'Lord of my desire'). *contra o meu desejo* (MS1932) the option that resolves it. Also in the Good Friday Tract. |

| circúitus (noun, *caput circúitus eórum*) | cerco (*A cabeça do seu cerco*) | open | Ps 139:10 (L&S 'a going round, a circling'); verbless as the Latin; the ambiguity reader found it opaque — as the Latin is (DRB 'the head of them compassing me about'). Kept apart from *in circúitu → ao redor*. |

| *ne forte* | para que acaso não (*para que acaso não se exaltem*) | open | Ps 139:9 (μήποτε). Draft 1 *para que não* dropped *forte*; the v1 Latinist and stylist both asked it back; *acaso* taken over *porventura* (longer, bookish). Cf. 78:10, 90:12. |
formulas: | *V. Éripe me, Dómine, ab hómine malo. R. A viro iníquo éripe me* (139:2; Preces feriales at Prime, Passiontide None, Major/Matutinum Special — grep; responsory form *… líbera me*, Quad5-2) · *Custódi me, Dómine, de manu peccatóris: et ab homínibus iníquis éripe me* (139:5; Offertory of Tuesday in Holy Week, Quad6-2) | *V. Arrancai-me, Senhor, do homem mau. R. Do homem iníquo arrancai-me* · *Guardai-me, Senhor, da mão do pecador: e dos homens iníquos arrancai-me* | open — Ps 139 (the erípere row; the responsory's *líbera me* → *livrai-me*) |

| *Ne derelínquas me, * Dómine, virtus salútis meæ* (139:9 + 139:8; Thursday Vespers antiphon, Psalmi major [Day5 Vespera]) · *Inténde in adjutórium meum, * Dómine, virtus salútis meæ* (Matins antiphon; 37:23 with this psalm's phrase) | *Não me abandoneis, * Senhor, poder da minha salvação* · *… Senhor, poder da minha salvação* | open — Ps 139 (virtus → poder; the second half of the Matins antiphon hangs on the *Inténde* row and D40) |
